correctness.rationale: After imposing exchange symmetry, subtracting the two cleared equilibrium equations gives exactly \((x_1-x_2)(A(x_1+x_2)+C)=0\). The diagonal branch has one positive root. Every off-diagonal equilibrium must have fixed positive sum \(S=a_1/d-K\) and product \(P=a_0/[d(1/L-1/K)]\), and conversely the two roots of \(t^2-St+P\) satisfy both equilibrium equations. Positive distinct roots are therefore equivalent to \(a_1>dK\), \(L<K\), and \(S^2>4P\). Equality and sign-boundary cases were checked separately. Both symmetric examples in the source are reproduced numerically. The global stability conclusion is invoked only in the strict three-distinct-equilibrium regime, exactly where the source theorem applies.

value.rationale: The source's main theorem makes the existence of three distinct positive equilibria the decisive hypothesis for global bistability, but leaves that hypothesis parameter-implicit. The new classification turns it into a sharp, interpretable design criterion for the natural exchange-symmetric family, identifies the exact symmetry-breaking boundary, explains both published examples, and subsumes the published equal-binding monostability special case. This is a motivated structural classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
